sources.title: Buddhist Non-Self: The No-Owner's Manual
limitations: Philosophical reconstruction of Buddhist positions is not empirical proof that non-self is ontologically true.
Buddhist traditions contain multiple interpretations of personhood and selfhood.

sources.title: Reconstructing and deconstructing the self: cognitive mechanisms in meditation practice
limitations: The article proposes a cognitive framework and synthesizes evidence rather than constituting a single decisive experiment.
Changes in self-related processing do not establish the metaphysical non-existence of a self.

sources.title: Self-awareness, self-regulation, and self-transcendence (S-ART): a framework for understanding the neurobiological mechanisms of mindfulness
limitations: S-ART is an integrative framework, not direct proof of a particular ontology of mind.
Self-transcendence as a psychological construct must not be equated with post-mortem survival or a nonlocal mind.

sources.title: Meditation experience is associated with differences in default mode network activity and connectivity
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
limitations: Group differences and task-related neuroimaging associations do not establish causation for all observed traits.
Default-mode-network activity is not a direct measure of an enduring metaphysical self.
Meditation-related neural differences do not establish consciousness independent of brain function.

sources.title: Physicalism
limitations: Reference synthesis of philosophical arguments; not an experimental verdict that physicalism is true.

sources.title: Dualism
limitations: Reference synthesis of philosophical positions; possibility and argumentative coherence are not empirical confirmation.

sources.title: Panpsychism
limitations: Reference synthesis of a family of metaphysical positions; philosophical motivation is not empirical confirmation of ubiquitous mentality.

claims.text: A 2011 fMRI study reported differences in default-mode-network activity and connectivity between experienced meditators and meditation-naive controls during several meditation conditions.
limitations: The observation concerns measured neural activity under studied conditions, not the existence or non-existence of a metaphysical self.
claims.uncertainty: The extent to which training, selection effects, task strategy and other factors explain group differences remains bounded by the study design.

claims.text: Contemplative-science frameworks describe meditation as capable of modifying attention, self-related processing, self-regulation and experiences described as self-transcendence.
limitations: Framework constructs summarize proposed mechanisms and evidence; they are not direct measurements of metaphysical reality.
claims.uncertainty: Different meditation practices, populations and operational definitions of self-processing may yield different effects.

claims.text: A major Buddhist philosophical strand can be reconstructed as denying an independently existing owner-self while treating the person in reductionist or conventional terms.
provenance: scholarly philosophical analysis of Buddhist non-self positions
limitations: This records a philosophical interpretation and tradition-level position, not an experimentally established ontology.
claims.uncertainty: Buddhist schools and scholars differ in how non-self, personhood and conventional reality are interpreted.

claims.text: Physicalist approaches hold, in differing formulations, that mental facts depend on or are wholly grounded in the physical; if such a view is correct, post-mortem continuation would require an account consistent with that dependence.
limitations: Physicalism is a philosophical position with multiple formulations and active objections; this record does not treat it as an empirical verdict.
claims.uncertainty: No formulation in this batch independently resolves the metaphysics of consciousness or post-mortem continuation.

claims.text: Dualist approaches hold that the mental and physical are fundamentally distinct in some respect, leaving conceptual room for forms of mind-body independence while facing questions about interaction, causal closure and evidence.
limitations: Conceptual room for independence does not establish that consciousness actually survives irreversible biological death.
claims.uncertainty: Competing varieties of dualism make different ontological and causal commitments.

claims.text: Panpsychist approaches treat mentality as fundamental and widespread in nature, offering an alternative to standard physicalism and dualism but not by themselves specifying whether an individual person's consciousness survives death.
limitations: Fundamental or ubiquitous mentality does not entail persistence of autobiographical identity, memory or an individual stream of consciousness.
claims.uncertainty: Panpsychism is a family of philosophical positions with unresolved combination and individuation problems.

batch_conclusion.statement: Batch 4 separates three layers that are often conflated: empirical observations of meditation-associated self-processing and neural activity, contemplative or Buddhist interpretations of selfhood, and competing metaphysical positions in philosophy of mind. None of these layers independently establishes either post-mortem continuation or its impossibility.
